family_title: Structured update shapes: Kronecker, Hadamard, tensor networks, high-rank, circulant, sparse+low-rank, Monarch

methods.name: LoHa
methods.paper_title: FedPara: Low-Rank Hadamard Product for Communication-Efficient Federated Learning
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \gamma\,(B_1A_1)\odot(B_2A_2),\quad B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ (k=1,2),\ \gamma=\alpha/r;\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ A_1,A_2,B_1,B_2\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: any linear or convolutional layer; popular on Stable Diffusion UNet/text-encoder (LyCORIS)
methods.structure: Hadamard (entrywise) product of two rank-r matrices; \mathrm{rank}(\Delta W)\le r^2 (FedPara Prop. 1) at the parameter cost of a rank-2r LoRA. Equivalently (B_1\odot_r B_2)(A_1^{\top}\odot_r A_2^{\top})^{\top}: a rank-r^2 factorization through row-wise Khatri-Rao products. Conv kernels can use a Tucker-style core variant (FedPara Prop. 3, use_effective_conv2d).
methods.mergeable_reason: ΔW is an explicit dense d_out x d_in matrix that can be added to W_0 after training.
methods.identity_at_init: HF PEFT: three factors Kaiming-uniform and one (hada_w2_b) zero so ΔW = 0; the original LyCORIS code uses normal init with one factor zeroed.
methods.key_idea: Entrywise-multiplying two low-rank matrices multiplies their ranks, so a LoRA-sized budget yields an update of rank up to r^2. Proposed for communication-efficient federated learning (FedPara) and turned into a fine-tuning adapter by LyCORIS.
methods.results_note: FedPara matches original-layer accuracy with 3-10x lower federated communication; as a PEFT adapter LoHa is benchmarked mainly for text-to-image customization in the LyCORIS study (ICLR 2024).

relations.note: each Hadamard factor is a LoRA product BA
sibling LyCORIS adapter: Hadamard vs Kronecker product of factors
HiRA replaces one trainable Hadamard factor by the frozen W_0
the Hadamard product of two low-rank matrices factors through row-wise Khatri-Rao products

methods.name: HiRA
methods.paper_title: HiRA: Parameter-Efficient Hadamard High-Rank Adaptation for Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + W_0\odot(BA) = W_0\odot(\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\top}+BA),\quad B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ A,B\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: any linear layer of an LLM (attention and MLP projections)
methods.structure: Entrywise (Hadamard) modulation of the frozen W_0 by a rank-r matrix; \mathrm{rank}(\Delta W)\le \mathrm{rank}(W_0)\cdot r, so the update is generically high-rank. Equivalently an additive update \Delta W = W_0\odot BA.
methods.mergeable_reason: W_0 ⊙ (BA) is a dense matrix of W_0's shape and is folded into W_0 after training.
methods.identity_at_init: One factor zero-initialized, the other Kaiming (paper: A = 0, B Kaiming in its AB notation; HF PEFT: B = 0), so ΔW = 0.
methods.key_idea: Reuse the pretrained weight itself as one Hadamard factor: modulating W_0 entrywise by a low-rank matrix gives high-rank updates aligned with W_0 at LoRA's parameter cost.
methods.results_note: Reported gains over LoRA and its variants on commonsense reasoning, dialogue generation and mathematical reasoning with LLaMA-family models (ICLR 2025 oral).

relations.note: same parameter budget r(d_in+d_out), but rank no longer bounded by r
LoHa learns both Hadamard factors; HiRA freezes one to W_0

methods.name: ABBA
methods.full_name: ABBA-Adapters (learnable Hadamard product of two low-rank matrices)
methods.paper_title: ABBA-Adapters: Efficient and Expressive Fine-Tuning of Foundation Models
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{r_1r_2}}\,(B_1A_1)\odot(B_2A_2) = W_0 + \frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{r_1r_2}}\,(B_1\odot_r B_2)(A_1^{\top}\odot_r A_2^{\top})^{\top},\quad B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r_k},\ A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{r_k\times d_{in}};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ B_1,A_1,B_2,A_2\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: any linear layer of an LLM
methods.structure: Hadamard product of two independently learnable rank-r_1 and rank-r_2 matrices (rank \le r_1r_2), executed without materialising \Delta W via the row-wise Khatri-Rao identity (B_1A_1)\odot(B_2A_2)=(B_1\odot_r B_2)(A_1^{\top}\odot_r A_2^{\top})^{\top}; rank-stabilised scale \alpha/\sqrt{r_1r_2}.
methods.mergeable_reason: The product is an ordinary dense matrix that can be added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: (B_1,A_1) initialised from the top-r_1 truncated SVD of W_0; B_2 = 0 and A_2 Kaiming-uniform, so ΔW = 0 at init.
methods.key_idea: Make both Hadamard factors learnable (HiRA fixes one to W_0), anchor one to the principal subspace of W_0, and use a rank-stabilising scale; the Khatri-Rao trick keeps memory at LoRA level.
methods.results_note: Reports state-of-the-art results on arithmetic and commonsense reasoning benchmarks across multiple LLMs, outperforming LoRA, HiRA and other PEFT baselines.

relations.note: HiRA is the case where the first Hadamard factor is frozen to W_0
same function class (B_1A_1)⊙(B_2A_2) as LoHa; differs in SVD-anchored init and √(r1 r2) scaling
matched parameter budget, rank up to r_1 r_2

methods.name: LoKr
methods.paper_title: Navigating Text-To-Image Customization: From LyCORIS Fine-Tuning to Model Evaluation
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \gamma\,C\otimes(BA),\quad C\in\mathbb{R}^{u_p\times u_q},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{v_p\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times v_q},\ u_pv_p=d_{out},\ u_qv_q=d_{in};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ C,B,A\ \text{trained (C optionally factorized: decompose\_both)}
methods.locus: any linear or convolutional layer; widely used for diffusion-model customization
methods.structure: Kronecker product of a small dense block C with a low-rank block BA: \mathrm{rank}(\Delta W)=\mathrm{rank}(C)\,\mathrm{rank}(BA)\le \min(u_p,u_q)\,r. Block sizes set by the factor hyperparameter f (u_p = largest divisor of d_out not exceeding min(f, sqrt(d_out))).
methods.mergeable_reason: C ⊗ (BA) is materialised as a dense matrix of W_0's shape and added to it.
methods.identity_at_init: HF PEFT zero-initializes the left Kronecker factor C (lokr_w1) and Kaiming-initializes the right factors, so ΔW = 0.
methods.key_idea: Ranks multiply under the Kronecker product, so a tiny dense block times a low-rank block gives a high-rank, block-structured update with very few parameters.
methods.results_note: Evaluated alongside LoRA and LoHa in the LyCORIS study of Stable Diffusion customization, which reports method-dependent trade-offs in fidelity, diversity and controllability rather than a single winner.

relations.note: with the right factor left unfactorized LoKr is exactly KronA's A⊗B
sibling LyCORIS adapter
the right Kronecker factor is a LoRA product

methods.name: KronA
methods.paper_title: KronA: Parameter Efficient Tuning with Kronecker Adapter
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + s\,(A_k\otimes B_k),\quad A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{a_1\times a_2},\ B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{b_1\times b_2},\ a_1b_1=d_{out},\ a_2b_2=d_{in};\quad \Delta W x = s\,\mathrm{vec}(B_k X A_k^{\top}),\ X=\mathrm{mat}(x)\in\mathbb{R}^{b_2\times a_2};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ A_k,B_k\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: parallel to attention/FFN weight matrices (KronA); KronA^B and KronA^B_res sit parallel to the whole FFN block
methods.structure: Single Kronecker product of two dense small factors; \mathrm{rank}(A_k\otimes B_k)=\mathrm{rank}(A_k)\,\mathrm{rank}(B_k), reaching full rank with O(\sqrt{d_{in}d_{out}}) parameters; forward pass by the vec-trick without materialising \Delta W.
methods.mergeable_reason: The weight-parallel KronA merges into W_0; the block-parallel KronA^B / KronA^B_res variants wrap a nonlinear FFN block and cannot be merged.
methods.identity_at_init: One factor zero-initialized and the other Kaiming-uniform (a = sqrt(5)); the paper reports zero-init of one factor markedly improves results.
methods.key_idea: Replace LoRA's low-rank product by a Kronecker product, which is full-rank-capable for the same tiny budget and cheap to apply via reshaping.
methods.results_note: On GLUE with T5-base, KronA variants outperform LoRA, adapters and Compacter at comparable budgets, with KronA^B_res the strongest (at extra inference latency).

relations.note: LoKr with an unfactorized right factor
rank-unbounded alternative at similar parameter count
Compacter uses a sum of n Kronecker products inside adapters

methods.name: PHM-Adapter
methods.paper_title: Compacter: Efficient Low-Rank Hypercomplex Adapter Layers
methods.formula_latex: h \leftarrow h + U\,\mathrm{GeLU}(Dh),\quad D=\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_i^{D}\otimes B_i^{D},\ U=\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_i^{U}\otimes B_i^{U},\ A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n},\ B_i^{D}\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{r}{n}\times\frac{d}{n}},\ B_i^{U}\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d}{n}\times\frac{r}{n}};\ \text{backbone frozen, adapters trained}
methods.locus: bottleneck adapters after the attention and feed-forward sublayers (Houlsby placement)
methods.structure: Bottleneck MLP inserted serially with residual connection whose down/up projections are PHM layers: sums of n Kronecker products (Kronecker rank \le n, i.e. rank \le n after Van Loan-Pitsianis rearrangement), reducing parameters by about 1/n.
methods.mergeable_reason: The adapter contains a GeLU nonlinearity in a new serial branch, so it cannot be folded into existing weights.
methods.identity_at_init: No exact zero-init guarantee is stated in the method section; like Houlsby adapters it relies on the residual connection with small-initialized adapter weights.
methods.key_idea: Learn the 'multiplication rule' of an n-dimensional hypercomplex algebra: a dense projection becomes a sum of n Kronecker products, cutting adapter parameters by ~n.
methods.results_note: On GLUE with T5-base, PHM-Adapter (n = 12) trains 0.179% of parameters and is competitive with full fine-tuning and standard adapters.

relations.note: replaces the adapter's dense projections by PHM layers
Compacter shares A_i across layers and makes B_i low-rank

methods.name: Compacter
methods.full_name: Compacter (Compact Adapter with low-rank PHM layers)
methods.paper_title: Compacter: Efficient Low-Rank Hypercomplex Adapter Layers
methods.formula_latex: h \leftarrow h + \mathrm{LPHM}^{U}\big(\mathrm{GeLU}(\mathrm{LPHM}^{D}(h))\big),\quad \mathrm{LPHM}=\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_i\otimes(s_i t_i^{\top}),\ A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\ \text{shared by all adapters},\ s_i\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{k}{n}\times\rho},\ t_i\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{k'}{n}\times\rho}\ (\rho=1\ \text{default})
methods.locus: bottleneck adapters after attention and FFN sublayers (Compacter++: after the FFN only)
methods.structure: Adapter projections are sums of n Kronecker products of shared 'slow' n x n matrices A_i with layer-specific rank-\rho 'fast' matrices s_i t_i^{\top} (low-rank PHM, LPHM).
methods.mergeable_reason: Serial bottleneck adapter with a nonlinearity; adds inference latency and cannot be folded.
methods.identity_at_init: Not specified as an exact zero-init; relies on the adapter residual connection as in Houlsby adapters.
methods.key_idea: Combine hypercomplex (Kronecker-sum) layers, cross-layer sharing of the slow factors, and rank-one fast factors to bring adapter cost from O(kd) to O(k+d).
methods.results_note: On GLUE with T5-base, Compacter (0.073%) and Compacter++ (0.047% of parameters) perform on par with full fine-tuning and outperform it on SuperGLUE and in low-resource settings.

relations.note: adds cross-layer sharing of A_i and low-rank B_i
same insertion points and bottleneck design
both reach ~0.05-0.1% trainable parameters

methods.name: KAdaptation
methods.paper_title: Parameter-efficient Model Adaptation for Vision Transformers
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \sum_{i=1}^{n}A_i\otimes(u_iv_i^{\top}),\quad A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\ \text{(shared across layers)},\ u_i\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d_{out}}{n}\times r},\ v_i\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d_{in}}{n}\times r};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ A_i,u_i,v_i\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: ViT attention weight matrices (submodules selected by lowest local intrinsic dimension)
methods.structure: Low-rank PHM (sum of n Kronecker products of shared slow weights with low-rank fast weights) applied directly to the weight update \Delta W rather than to an inserted adapter.
methods.mergeable_reason: ΔW is a dense matrix added to frozen attention weights; the paper notes no added inference latency.
methods.identity_at_init: Not stated explicitly in the method section consulted; presumably one fast factor starts at zero so ΔW = 0 (unverified).
methods.key_idea: Choose where to adapt via the local intrinsic dimension of each ViT submodule, then express the update as a Compacter-style Kronecker sum so it merges like LoRA.
methods.results_note: Best accuracy/parameter trade-off among compared methods on 20 image-classification datasets few-shot and 7 datasets full-shot with CLIP ViTs.

relations.note: same LPHM parameterization, moved from inserted adapters to ΔW
mergeable additive update with Kronecker structure instead of plain low rank

methods.name: KRAdapter
methods.paper_title: Towards Higher Effective Rank in Parameter-efficient Fine-tuning using Khatri--Rao Product
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \alpha\,\big[U\odot_{KR}V\big]_{1:d_{out},\,:},\quad (U\odot_{KR}V)_{:,j}=U_{:,j}\otimes V_{:,j},\ U\in\mathbb{R}^{k_1\times d_{in}},\ V\in\mathbb{R}^{k_2\times d_{in}},\ k_1k_2\ge d_{out};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ U,V\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: linear layers of vision-language models and LLMs
methods.structure: Column-wise Kronecker (Khatri-Rao) product truncated to d_out rows; almost surely full column rank, with a heavier singular-value tail (higher effective rank) than Kronecker or low-rank updates.
methods.mergeable_reason: The Khatri-Rao product is a dense matrix of W_0's shape.
methods.identity_at_init: U zero-initialized and V randomly initialized, so ΔW = 0.
methods.key_idea: Target effective rank, not just algebraic rank: the Khatri-Rao product spreads energy over many singular directions at about the cost of a rank-16-32 LoRA.
methods.results_note: Reports gains on vision-language models up to 1B and LLMs up to 8B parameters, especially on unseen commonsense-reasoning tasks, with LoRA-level memory and compute.

relations.note: column-wise vs full Kronecker product; paper contrasts their spectra
same authors' alternative route to full-rank updates
matched budget, higher effective rank

methods.name: LoRETTA
methods.paper_title: LoRETTA: Low-Rank Economic Tensor-Train Adaptation for Ultra-Low-Parameter Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \mathrm{TT}(\Delta W_{up})\,\mathrm{TT}(\Delta W_{down}),\quad \Delta W_{up}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ \Delta W_{down}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ \mathrm{TT}(M)[a_1,\dots,a_D]=G^{1}_{a_1}G^{2}_{a_2}\cdots G^{D}_{a_D},\ G^{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{r_{i-1}\times k_i\times r_i}\ (\text{LoRETTA}_{rep});\ \text{TT cores trained}
methods.trainable_params: \sum_{i=1}^{D}r_{i-1}k_ir_i\ \text{for each of the two tensorized factors}
methods.locus: LoRETTA_rep: attention/MLP weight matrices (like LoRA); LoRETTA_adp: tensorized bottleneck adapters after attention and FFN sublayers
methods.structure: Each LoRA factor is reshaped into a D-way tensor and stored in tensor-train (MPS) format; the adapter variant tensorizes the up/down projections of a bottleneck adapter instead.
methods.mergeable_reason: LoRETTA_rep yields a dense ΔW that can be merged; LoRETTA_adp is a serial adapter with a nonlinearity and cannot.
methods.identity_at_init: All TT cores are Gaussian-initialized (a zero core would stall gradients); the noise injected by this random initialization is then compensated using the initialized weights so training starts from the pretrained function.
methods.key_idea: Push LoRA's parameter count down by another one to two orders of magnitude by storing its factors as tensor trains.
methods.results_note: Comparable or better than widely used PEFT methods with up to 100x fewer trainable parameters than LoRA/adapters on LLaMA-2-7B.

relations.note: tensorizes LoRA's two factors
TT-LoRA tensorizes the whole ΔW as a single tensor train
QuanTA uses a circuit-shaped tensor network instead of a TT chain

methods.name: TT-LoRA
methods.paper_title: Tensor Train Low-rank Approximation (TT-LoRA): Democratizing AI with Accelerated LLMs
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \alpha\,\mathrm{mat}\big(\mathcal{C}_1\times^{1}\mathcal{C}_2\times^{1}\cdots\times^{1}\mathcal{C}_D\big),\quad \mathcal{C}_i\in\mathbb{R}^{r_{i-1}\times k_i\times r_i},\ r_0=r_D=1,\ \textstyle\prod_i k_i=d_{out}d_{in};\quad y=W_0x+\alpha\,(\textstyle\prod_i\mathcal{C}_i)\,x;\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ \mathcal{C}_i\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: W_q and W_v attention projections
methods.structure: \Delta W reshaped into a D-way tensor held in tensor-train (MPS) format; the input is contracted core-by-core without reconstructing \Delta W.
methods.mergeable_reason: The TT cores can be contracted into a dense ΔW and added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Does not preserve the function: ΔW is drawn from a Gaussian and then TT-decomposed, so the adapted model differs from the base model at step 0.
methods.key_idea: Drop the LoRA matrix factorization altogether and represent the full update as one tensor train, contracted directly with the input for compression and lower latency.
methods.results_note: On BERT-family models (GLUE) and LLaMA-2/3, reports accuracy comparable to LoRA and other PEFT methods with substantially higher compression.

relations.note: extends LoRETTA's tensor-train idea to a single TT for ΔW
alternative factorization of ΔW

methods.name: LoTR
methods.paper_title: LoTR: Low Tensor Rank Weight Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W_s = W_{0,s} + \alpha\,A\,G_s\,B^{\top},\quad A\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times r}\ \text{shared by all layers } s,\ G_s\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r}\ \text{layer-specific};\ \delta\mathcal{W}=\mathcal{G}\times_1A\times_2B
methods.trainable_params: |\mathcal{W}|\,r^{2}+r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{for a stack of } |\mathcal{W}| \text{ equally shaped matrices}
methods.locus: a stack of same-type matrices across depth (e.g. all W_q, all W_v)
methods.structure: Tucker-2 decomposition of the 3-tensor of updates stacked over layers: shared left/right factor matrices with a per-layer r x r core.
methods.mergeable_reason: Each A G_s B^T is a dense update for its layer and can be added to W_{0,s}.
methods.identity_at_init: Core G = 0 with A, B ~ N(0,1) (found best among tested schemes), so ΔW = 0.
methods.key_idea: Share the column/row spaces of the update across all layers and only learn a tiny r x r mixing core per layer, so cost grows with depth as r^2 rather than r(d_in+d_out).
methods.results_note: Reports better parameter efficiency than LoRA, with savings that grow with model depth.

relations.note: same Tucker-2 form as FacT-TT (ΔW_i = UΣ_iV^T with shared U,V)
LoRA with an r x r core and cross-layer sharing of the outer factors
FLoRA uses an unshared per-layer Tucker core

methods.name: FacT
methods.paper_title: FacT: Factor-Tuning for Lightweight Adaptation on Vision Transformer
methods.formula_latex: \text{FacT-TT: }\Delta W_i = s\,U\Sigma_iV^{\top},\ U,V\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times r},\ \Sigma\in\mathbb{R}^{12L\times r\times r};\qquad \text{FacT-TK: }\Delta\mathcal{W}=s\,\mathcal{C}\times_1P\times_2U\times_3V,\ \mathcal{C}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r\times r},\ P\in\mathbb{R}^{12L\times r};\ W_0\ \text{frozen}
methods.locus: all d x d weight blocks of a ViT (W_q, W_k, W_v, W_o and the MLP matrices split into d x d blocks) stacked into a 12L x d x d tensor
methods.structure: The whole ViT is tensorized into one 12L x d x d tensor and its increment is held in a tensor-train (FacT-TT) or Tucker (FacT-TK) format; LoRA corresponds to the matrix-batch format.
methods.mergeable_reason: Factors are contracted into dense increments and absorbed into the weights before inference.
methods.identity_at_init: V zero-initialized and the other factors random, so ΔW = 0.
methods.key_idea: Exploit redundancy both within and across weight matrices by decomposing all increments of the network as one tensor.
methods.results_note: On VTAB-1K performs on par with NOAH while being 5x more parameter-efficient; an 8K-parameter version (0.01% of ViT-B) outperforms full fine-tuning, VPT and BitFit.

relations.note: the paper reads LoRA as the matrix-batch format of the same tensorized update
FacT-TT and LoTR share the Tucker-2 form with cross-layer U, V

methods.name: FLoRA (Tucker core)
methods.full_name: Low-rank core-space adaptation for N-dimensional parameter spaces
methods.paper_title: Maintaining Structural Integrity in Parameter Spaces for Parameter Efficient Fine-tuning
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + s\,\mathcal{G}\times_1A^{(1)}\times_2\cdots\times_NA^{(N)};\quad \text{linear: } W=W_0+s\,AGB^{\top},\ G\in\mathbb{R}^{r_1\times r_2},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r_1},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times r_2};\ \text{conv: }\Delta W=\mathcal{G}\times_1A\times_2B\times_3C\times_4D
methods.locus: linear and convolutional layers (ConvNeXt, DeBERTa, LLaMA-3, InternViT)
methods.structure: Tucker decomposition of \Delta W in its native N-D shape (a low-rank 'core space' with the same topology as the weight); for matrices it is the three-factor A G B^{\top}.
methods.mergeable_reason: The Tucker product is a dense tensor of the weight's shape.
methods.identity_at_init: Core G zero-initialized, factor matrices Gaussian, so ΔW = 0.
methods.key_idea: Do not flatten conv kernels into matrices: model the update with a Tucker core that keeps the kernel's spatial structure.
methods.results_note: Outperforms LoRA and DoRA on ConvNeXt-V2 detection/segmentation, DeBERTaV3 GLUE, LLaMA-3-8B commonsense reasoning and InternViT multimodal tasks.

relations.note: G = I recovers LoRA; for linear layers the function class equals rank-min(r1,r2) LoRA, so the gain is in N-D layers and optimization
LoTR shares the outer factors across layers
FacT-TK applies Tucker across layers instead of within a kernel

methods.name: LoRTA
methods.paper_title: LoRTA: Efficient Low Rank Tensor Adaptation of Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: \Delta W_{k,l,i}=A\,\mathrm{Diag}(C_H[k,:])\,\mathrm{Diag}(C_L[l,:])\,\mathrm{Diag}(C_M[i,:])\,B^{\top},\ \text{i.e. } \Delta\mathcal{W}=[\![A,B,C_H,C_L,C_M]\!],\quad A\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times r},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d}{H}\times r},\ C_H\in\mathbb{R}^{H\times r},\ C_L\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times r},\ C_M\in\mathbb{R}^{4\times r}
methods.locus: Q, K, V and output projections of every attention head in every layer
methods.structure: Rank-r CP (Candecomp/Parafac) model of the 5th-order tensor of all attention updates indexed by (input dim, head dim, head, layer, matrix type).
methods.mergeable_reason: Each slice of the CP tensor is a dense per-head update that can be added to its weight.
methods.identity_at_init: Not detailed in the sections consulted.
methods.key_idea: Share one CP model over heads, layers and Q/K/V/O so that parameters grow additively, not multiplicatively, in these dimensions.
methods.results_note: Reports performance comparable to LoRA with far fewer parameters on NLU, instruction tuning, preference optimization and protein-folding benchmarks.

relations.note: LoRTA Sec. 3 reads VeRA's frozen shared bases with per-layer diagonal scalings as a sum of CP models with frozen factors
CP across layers/heads vs Tucker-2 across layers
MetaTT uses a tensor train over the same index set

methods.name: MetaTT
methods.paper_title: MetaTT: A Global Tensor-Train Adapter for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: y = xW_{0,l,m} + \alpha\,x\,G_1\,G_2[l]\,G_3[m]\,G_4\ \ (\text{row-vector convention}),\quad G_1\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times r},\ G_2[l],G_3[m]\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r},\ G_4\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{out}}\ \ (\text{MetaTT-4D})
methods.locus: attention (and optionally MLP) projections of all layers; layer index l and matrix type m (and head h, task t) are TT modes
methods.structure: A single tensor train over (input, layer, matrix type, [head], [task], output) whose slices are the per-matrix updates; a DMRG-style sweep can adapt TT ranks during training.
methods.mergeable_reason: Middle cores can be contracted into G_1 or G_4 to give a dense per-matrix update.
methods.identity_at_init: Not detailed in the sections consulted.
methods.key_idea: One global adapter for the whole network: factorize the update tensor across depth and matrix type with a tensor train, borrowing DMRG rank adaptation from many-body physics.
methods.results_note: Reports substantial parameter reductions at competitive accuracy versus LoRA-style baselines, and competitive multi-task results with a task mode.

relations.note: LoTR's per-matrix core G_s factorizes here as G_2[l] G_3[m]
TT vs CP over the same layer/head/matrix modes

methods.name: QuanTA
methods.paper_title: QuanTA: Efficient High-Rank Fine-Tuning of LLMs with Quantum-Informed Tensor Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: y = W_0x + \mathcal{T}_{\theta}x - \mathcal{S}x,\quad \mathcal{T}_{\theta}=\prod_{\alpha}T^{(\alpha)},\ T^{(\alpha)}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{m}d_{n}\times d_{m}d_{n}}\ \text{acting on axes } (m(\alpha),n(\alpha)) \text{ of } x \text{ reshaped to } d_1\times\cdots\times d_N,\ \textstyle\prod_n d_n=d;\ \mathcal{S}=\mathcal{T}_{\theta_0}\ \text{frozen}
methods.locus: linear layers of LLMs (attention projections)
methods.structure: Circuit-shaped tensor network: the hidden vector is viewed as an N-qudit state and a sequence of two-axis 'gates' is applied (an einsum of small tensors); by the universality and rank-representation theorems it can express full-rank updates.
methods.mergeable_reason: The gate sequence is linear, so the full matrix T can be contracted and added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: A frozen copy S of the initial gates is subtracted (T_θ x - S x = 0 at step 0); S is then folded into W_0' = W_0 + S at no extra cost.
methods.key_idea: Borrow quantum-circuit structure (local two-qudit gates composed in sequence) to get high-rank updates with few parameters and without zero-initialized factors.
methods.results_note: Improves over LoRA and DoRA on commonsense and arithmetic reasoning with LLaMA-family models while using fewer trainable parameters.

relations.note: high-rank alternative at lower parameter count
different tensor-network topology (circuit vs train)

methods.name: Quantum-PEFT
methods.paper_title: Quantum-PEFT: Ultra parameter-efficient fine-tuning
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + U\Lambda V^{\top},\quad U=Q_P(\theta_U)\,I_{d_{out}\times K},\ V=Q_P(\theta_V)\,I_{d_{in}\times K},\ \Lambda=\mathrm{diag}(\lambda)\in\mathbb{R}^{K\times K},\ Q_P=\prod_{l=1}^{L}\Big(\mathrm{CZ}\text{-layer}\cdot\textstyle\bigotimes_{k=1}^{q}\mathrm{RY}(\theta_{k,l})\Big),\ q=\log_2 d;\ \theta_U,\theta_V,\lambda\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: same targets as LoRA (attention/linear layers of language and vision transformers)
methods.structure: SVD-form update whose orthogonal factors are quantum-circuit (Pauli) parameterizations: Kronecker products of 2 x 2 RY rotations interleaved with diagonal \pm1 CZ entanglers, so parameters grow logarithmically in d.
methods.mergeable_reason: U Λ V^T is a dense matrix that can be added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Not stated explicitly in the sections consulted (AdaLoRA-style SVD form; a zero diagonal Λ would give ΔW = 0).
methods.key_idea: Parameterize the singular-vector frames by a small quantum circuit, so trainable parameters scale like log d instead of d.
methods.results_note: Reports orders of magnitude fewer trainable parameters than the lowest-rank LoRA with competitive accuracy on language and vision transfer benchmarks.

relations.note: same UΛV^T SVD-form update
both build orthogonal matrices from products of sparse/Kronecker-structured factors
both quantum-circuit-inspired tensor networks

methods.name: MoRA
methods.full_name: High-rank updating with a square matrix
methods.paper_title: MoRA: High-Rank Updating for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: h = W_0x + f_{decomp}\big(M\,f_{comp}(x)\big),\quad M\in\mathbb{R}^{\hat r\times\hat r},\ \hat r=\big\lfloor\sqrt{(d_{in}+d_{out})\,r}\big\rfloor;\ \text{reshape variant: }\Delta W=I_{d/\hat r}\otimes M=\mathrm{diag}(M,\dots,M);\ \text{RoPE variant: }\Delta W=\mathrm{diag}(P^{1},\dots,P^{n}),\ P^{i}=M\ \text{rotated by block rotation } R_{\theta,i}
methods.locus: all linear layers of LLMs
methods.structure: A single trainable square matrix sandwiched between fixed, non-parameterized compression/decompression operators (truncation, row/column sharing, reshaping, RoPE-style rotations); the reshape variant is a Kronecker product with the identity, i.e. a block-diagonal matrix with tied blocks of rank up to \hat r each.
methods.mergeable_reason: The fixed operators are linear, so ΔW can be formed explicitly and merged like LoRA.
methods.identity_at_init: M = 0 (a single matrix can be zero-initialized without stalling gradients).
methods.key_idea: Spend the LoRA parameter budget on one square matrix to maximize the rank of ΔW, which matters for knowledge-memorizing tasks.
methods.results_note: Outperforms LoRA on memory-intensive tasks (UUID memorization, continual pretraining) and is comparable on instruction tuning and math reasoning.

relations.note: freezing KronA's left factor to I gives the reshape variant I ⊗ M
block-diagonal with tied full-rank blocks vs untied low-rank blocks
same parameter budget, much higher rank

methods.name: MELoRA
methods.paper_title: MELoRA: Mini-Ensemble Low-Rank Adapters for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \mathrm{diag}(B_1A_1,\dots,B_nA_n)=W_0+\bigoplus_{i=1}^{n}B_iA_i,\quad A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{r}{n}\times\frac{d_{in}}{n}},\ B_i\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d_{out}}{n}\times\frac{r}{n}};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ A_i,B_i\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: attention/MLP linear layers (as LoRA)
methods.structure: Block-diagonal direct sum of n independent mini-LoRAs acting on disjoint feature slices; rank is the sum of block ranks, so rank r is reached with n times fewer parameters than LoRA.
methods.mergeable_reason: The block-diagonal ΔW is a dense matrix of W_0's shape.
methods.identity_at_init: A_i Gaussian and B_i = 0, as in LoRA.
methods.key_idea: Concatenating mini-LoRAs along the diagonal adds their ranks instead of sharing a bottleneck, trading cross-block interactions for rank per parameter.
methods.results_note: Compared with LoRA, better results with 8x fewer trainable parameters on natural language understanding and 36x fewer on instruction following.

relations.note: GraLoRA with all off-diagonal blocks removed
BD-LoRA with both factors block-diagonal and aligned
MoRe's Monarch product with identity permutations
higher rank per parameter

methods.name: GraLoRA
methods.paper_title: GraLoRA: Granular Low-Rank Adaptation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \tfrac{\alpha}{r}\big[\,B_{ij}A_{ij}^{\top}\,\big]_{i,j=1}^{k},\quad A_{ij}\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d_{in}}{k}\times\frac{r}{k}},\ B_{ij}\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d_{out}}{k}\times\frac{r}{k}};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ A_{ij},B_{ij}\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: any linear layer of LLMs
methods.structure: k x k grid of independent rank-(r/k) blocks, equivalently B_G A_G^{\top} with sparse block-structured factors; rank up to k r at LoRA's parameter count; Hybrid GraLoRA adds a plain LoRA term.
methods.mergeable_reason: The block matrix is an ordinary dense update.
methods.identity_at_init: A Kaiming-uniform and B = 0 (HF PEFT), so ΔW = 0.
methods.key_idea: Partition the weight into sub-blocks with their own small adapters so that input outlier channels only perturb local gradients and effective rank grows by k.
methods.results_note: Up to +8.5% absolute Pass@1 on HumanEval+ over LoRA, with consistent gains on commonsense reasoning across model sizes and ranks.

relations.note: k = 1 recovers LoRA
MELoRA keeps only the diagonal blocks
both raise rank at LoRA's budget

methods.name: BD-LoRA
methods.paper_title: Block-Diagonal LoRA for Eliminating Communication Overhead in Tensor Parallel LoRA Serving
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA,\ \ B=\mathrm{diag}(B_1,\dots,B_N)\ (\text{column-sharded: } W_q,W_k,W_v,\text{up},\text{gate})\ \text{or}\ A=\mathrm{diag}(A_1,\dots,A_N)\ (\text{row-sharded: } W_o,\text{down}),\ N=\text{tensor-parallel degree}
methods.locus: attention and MLP projections, with the block-diagonal factor chosen to match the layer's tensor-parallel sharding
methods.structure: LoRA with one factor constrained to a block-diagonal matrix aligned with the tensor-parallel shards, so the adapter factors through a direct sum of N per-device maps and needs no extra all-gather/all-reduce.
methods.mergeable_reason: It is a constrained LoRA, so BA can be merged; the design target is unmerged multi-adapter serving.
methods.identity_at_init: Standard LoRA initialization (B = 0), so ΔW = 0.
methods.key_idea: Choose the shape of the adapter to fit the hardware sharding: block-diagonal factors make multi-LoRA serving communication-free with almost no loss in quality per parameter.
methods.results_note: Matches LoRA's downstream quality at similar parameter counts and gives up to 1.79x end-to-end serving speed-up over S-LoRA tensor parallelism for Llama-3.1-8B on eight A100 GPUs.

relations.note: LoRA with a block-diagonal constraint on one factor
MELoRA constrains both factors block-diagonally

methods.name: MoRe
methods.paper_title: MoRe Fine-Tuning with 10x Fewer Parameters
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + P_1\,L\,P_2\,R,\quad L=\mathrm{diag}(L_1,\dots,L_N),\ R=\mathrm{diag}(R_1,\dots,R_N),\ L_j\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d_{out}}{N}\times r_{blk}},\ R_j\in\mathbb{R}^{r_{blk}\times\frac{d_{in}}{N}},\ P_1,P_2\ \text{fixed permutations};\ L,R\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: attention/MLP linear layers
methods.structure: Rectangular low-rank Monarch matrix: block-diagonal, permutation, block-diagonal, permutation; rank up to N r_{blk}; N = 1 recovers LoRA and the class contains butterfly matrices.
methods.mergeable_reason: The Monarch product is a dense matrix that W absorbs before inference.
methods.identity_at_init: Not specified in the paper; a LoRA-style zero factor would give ΔW = 0 (unverified).
methods.key_idea: Search over a hardware-efficient structured matrix family (Monarch) instead of fixing low rank, gaining rank per parameter with almost no hyperparameter tuning (N = 4).
methods.results_note: Reported to be more parameter-efficient and accurate than state-of-the-art PEFT methods on a range of tasks and models, using as little as 5% of LoRA's parameters.

relations.note: N = 1 gives LoRA
identity permutations give MELoRA's block-diagonal update
BOFT uses orthogonal butterfly factors multiplicatively; MoRe uses non-orthogonal Monarch factors additively

methods.name: C³A
methods.paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning via Circular Convolution
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \mathcal{C}_{blk}(\Delta w),\quad \mathcal{C}_{blk}(\Delta w)=\big[\mathcal{C}(\Delta w_{ij})\big]_{i\le d_{out}/b,\ j\le d_{in}/b},\ \mathcal{C}(w)=F^{-1}\mathrm{diag}(Fw)\,F\in\mathbb{R}^{b\times b};\ \Delta W x\ \text{computed with FFTs};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ \Delta w_{ij}\in\mathbb{R}^{b}\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: linear layers (nn.Linear only in HF PEFT)
methods.structure: Block-circulant matrix: each b x b block is a circular-convolution kernel, diagonalized by the DFT; a block's rank equals its number of non-zero Fourier coefficients (up to b), so \mathrm{rank}(\Delta W) can reach \min(d_{in},d_{out}) independently of the parameter count.
methods.mergeable_reason: The block-circulant matrix can be materialized and added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: HF PEFT default is Xavier-uniform (not a no-op); init_weights=True zero-initializes the kernels for an exact no-op. The paper finds results insensitive to the initialization scheme.
methods.key_idea: Learn convolution kernels instead of low-rank factors: circulant structure gives high rank with FFT-speed, LoRA-like memory.
methods.results_note: Consistently outperforms LoRA and its variants across fine-tuning tasks (GLUE, instruction tuning, vision) while being efficient in compute and memory.

relations.note: a circulant matrix is diagonal in the Fourier basis (convolution theorem)
high-rank alternative at comparable cost
positioned as more efficient than random-projection methods

methods.name: RoSA
methods.paper_title: RoSA: Accurate Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning via Robust Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + BA + S,\quad \mathrm{supp}(S)\subseteq\Omega,\ |\Omega|=\delta\,d_{out}d_{in},\ \Omega=\mathrm{TopK}\Big(\textstyle\sum_{s\in\mathcal{D}_M}\big(\nabla_W\mathcal{L}(s)\big)^{2}\Big);\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ A,B,S|_{\Omega}\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: all linear layers of LLMs (LLaMA-2)
methods.structure: Robust-PCA-shaped update: low-rank plus fixed-support sparse matrix; the support is the top-\delta fraction of accumulated squared gradients on a small mask-generation set.
methods.mergeable_reason: Both components are explicit matrices of W_0's shape and can be added.
methods.identity_at_init: Low-rank part initialized as in LoRA (one factor zero) and sparse values start at zero, so ΔW = 0.
methods.key_idea: Full fine-tuning updates are approximately low-rank plus sparse, so learning both components jointly recovers more of full fine-tuning's accuracy than either alone.
methods.results_note: Outperforms LoRA, pure sparse fine-tuning and other hybrids at equal budget on GSM8k, ViGGO and SQL generation with LLaMA-2-7B, sometimes matching full fine-tuning.

relations.note: adds a sparse component to LoRA
with no low-rank part RoSA is gradient-masked sparse adaptation as in SHiRA-Grad
DSEE picks its sparse support by robust PCA of W_0 rather than gradients

methods.name: DSEE
methods.paper_title: DSEE: Dually Sparsity-embedded Efficient Tuning of Pre-trained Language Models
methods.formula_latex: W = \big(W_0 + UV + \mathcal{P}_{\Omega}(S)\big)\odot \mathcal{M},\quad U\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ V\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ \Omega=\mathrm{supp}\Big(\arg\min_{\mathrm{rank}\le r,\ \mathrm{card}(S')\le c}\|W_0-U'V'-S'\|_F^{2}\Big),\ \mathcal{M}\ \text{optional pruning mask}
methods.locus: attention weight matrices of BERT, RoBERTa and GPT-2
methods.structure: Low-rank plus sparse-residual update whose sparse support comes from a robust-PCA (GreBsmo) decomposition of W_0, combined with unstructured or structured pruning of the resulting weights for inference efficiency.
methods.mergeable_reason: UV + P_Ω(S) is added to W_0; the result can additionally be pruned with the mask.
methods.identity_at_init: V = 0 and S = 0, so ΔW = 0 at init.
methods.key_idea: Exploit sparsity twice: sparse-plus-low-rank structure in the update for parameter efficiency, and sparse final weights for inference efficiency.
methods.results_note: On BERT, saves about 25% inference FLOPs with 0.5% trainable parameters at comparable downstream performance.

relations.note: adds a sparse residual and weight pruning to a LoRA-style update
both sparse-plus-low-rank updates
sparse update component

methods.name: SHiRA
methods.paper_title: Sparse High Rank Adapters
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + M\odot S,\quad M\in\{0,1\}^{d_{out}\times d_{in}}\ \text{fixed},\ \|M\|_0=r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ (\approx1\text{-}2\%),\ S\ \text{trained only on } \mathrm{supp}(M)
methods.locus: linear layers of LVMs (e.g. SDXL) and LLMs (e.g. LLaMA)
methods.structure: Static sparse coordinate mask on W_0 (implemented by gradient masking or as a separate sparse delta); masks: Struct (rows/columns plus diagonal), Rand, weight-magnitude, gradient, SNIP; the sparse update is generically high-rank.
methods.mergeable_reason: Only 1-2% of entries of W_0 are overwritten, so the adapter merges (and switches) by a sparse scatter.
methods.identity_at_init: S zero-initialized (HF PEFT), so W = W_0.
methods.key_idea: Fine-tune 1-2% of the base weights directly: sparse updates are high-rank, switch quickly on device and interfere less when fused.
methods.results_note: Outperforms LoRA on LVM and LLM adaptation while enabling rapid adapter switching and multi-adapter fusion; the PEFT implementation uses up to 16% less peak GPU memory than LoRA.

relations.note: RoSA without its low-rank part
sparse update of pretrained weights with a fixed mask
same parameter count r(d_in+d_out), high rank

methods.name: Sine-LoRA
methods.paper_title: Efficient Learning With Sine-Activated Low-rank Matrices
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \tfrac{1}{g}\sin(\omega\,BA),\quad \sin\ \text{entrywise},\ \omega\ \text{(frequency)},\ g\ \text{(gain) fixed},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: LoRA/DoRA target layers in LLMs and ViTs (also NeRF and 3D-shape networks)
methods.structure: Entrywise sinusoid of a rank-r matrix; the rank of \sin(\omega\,BA) grows with \omega (the paper gives a lower bound in terms of \omega), so the update is no longer low-rank.
methods.mergeable_reason: sin(ωBA)/g is a dense matrix computable after training and addable to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: With LoRA's B = 0 initialization, sin(0) = 0 so ΔW = 0.
methods.key_idea: A fixed high-frequency entrywise nonlinearity raises the rank of a low-rank parameterization for free.
methods.results_note: Improves LoRA and DoRA at equal parameter count across ViT, LLM (e.g. LLaMA-3-8B commonsense reasoning, GLUE), NeRF and 3D-shape tasks.

relations.note: drop-in modification of LoRA's product
both raise rank with entrywise operations on low-rank matrices

methods.name: MiSS
methods.paper_title: MiSS: Revisiting the Trade-off in LoRA with an Efficient Shard-Sharing Structure
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \mathrm{expand}(D)=W_0+E\,D,\quad E=\mathrm{diag}(\mathbf{1}_{s_1},\dots,\mathbf{1}_{s_N})\in\{0,1\}^{d_{out}\times N}\ \text{fixed},\ D\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times d_{in}};\ \text{efficient form: }\Delta W=D'\,(\mathbf{1}_{d_{in}/r}^{\top}\otimes I_r),\ D'\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}
methods.locus: any linear layer of LLMs
methods.structure: A single small trainable matrix replicated across shards by a fixed 0/1 replication operator (a Kronecker product with an all-ones vector); rank \le N (or r).
methods.mergeable_reason: The expanded matrix is dense and is added to W_0.
methods.key_idea: Replace one LoRA factor by a fixed shard-replication operator: a single zero-initialized matrix gives fast init, low memory and LoRA-level accuracy.
methods.results_note: Reports a favorable trade-off between performance, memory, initialization overhead and speed versus LoRA, PiSSA and DoRA on LLaMA-2, Mistral, RWKV and Qwen3.

relations.note: LoRA with one factor frozen to the 0/1 replication matrix
both freeze part of the factorization to cut trainable parameters

papers.title: Beyond Fully-Connected Layers with Quaternions: Parameterization of Hypercomplex Multiplications with 1/n Parameters
papers.claim: A dense layer can be parameterized as a sum of n Kronecker products, W = Σ_i A_i ⊗ B_i, which subsumes the quaternion Hamilton product and learns arbitrary n-D hypercomplex multiplication rules with about 1/n of the parameters.
papers.relevance: The algebraic origin of PHM-Adapter, Compacter and KAdaptation; makes 'Kronecker rank' an explicit design axis, the Kronecker analogue of LoRA's matrix rank.

papers.title: Approximation with Kronecker Products
papers.venue: Linear Algebra for Large Scale and Real-Time Applications (NATO ASI Series, vol. 232), Springer
papers.claim: The nearest Kronecker product (and sum of Kronecker products) to a matrix is obtained from an SVD of a rearrangement of that matrix, so Kronecker rank equals ordinary rank after rearrangement.
papers.relevance: Shows that Kronecker-sum adapters (PHM, KAdaptation, KronA) are low-rank adapters in a different matricization, a single invariant that organizes the whole 'shape' family.

papers.title: Tensor-Train Decomposition
papers.claim: Introduces the tensor-train (TT) format with SVD-based TT-SVD and rounding algorithms, storing a d-way tensor with O(d n r^2) parameters.
papers.relevance: Mathematical basis of LoRETTA, TT-LoRA, FacT-TT and MetaTT; TT is the simplest non-trivial tensor network (a linear chain).

papers.title: Tensor Decompositions and Applications
papers.claim: Standard survey of CP (CANDECOMP/PARAFAC), Tucker and related decompositions, mode-n products and their algorithms.
papers.relevance: Reference notation for the Tucker (LoTR, FLoRA, FacT-TK) and CP (LoRTA) adapters and for VeRA-style shared bases read as CP models.

papers.title: Low-Rank Tensor Networks for Dimensionality Reduction and Large-Scale Optimization Problems: Perspectives and Challenges PART 1
papers.venue: Foundations and Trends in Machine Learning 9(4-5)
papers.claim: Monograph on tensor networks (TT, hierarchical Tucker, etc.) with graphical (string-diagram) notation for contractions and their use in large-scale optimization.
papers.relevance: Supplies the diagrammatic calculus in which every 'shape' adapter is a string diagram of trainable and frozen boxes, the natural bridge to a categorical (monoidal) treatment.

papers.title: Monarch: Expressive Structured Matrices for Efficient and Accurate Training
papers.claim: Monarch matrices, products of two block-diagonal matrices interleaved with permutations, are hardware-efficient, express many standard transforms, and admit an analytically optimal projection of a dense matrix.
papers.relevance: Structured-matrix foundation of MoRe; also explains MELoRA/GraLoRA/BD-LoRA as block-diagonal (direct-sum) shapes and BOFT's butterflies as the orthogonal counterpart.

papers.title: Compute Better Spent: Replacing Dense Layers with Structured Matrices
papers.claim: Different structured matrix families need different initialization scales and learning rates (derived via muP); the Block Tensor-Train (BTT) family, which contains Monarch, beats dense layers per unit of compute.
papers.relevance: Explains why shape-based adapters need method-specific scalings (e.g. ABBA's rank-stabilized scale, C3A's large learning rate) and gives a compute-optimal lens for comparing shapes.

papers.title: LoRA Learns Less and Forgets Less
papers.claim: On code and math, LoRA substantially underperforms full fine-tuning but forgets less; full fine-tuning learns perturbations whose rank is 10-100x larger than typical LoRA configurations.
papers.relevance: Empirical motivation for the high-rank branch of the shape family (MoRA, HiRA, ABBA, C3A, QuanTA, GraLoRA, SHiRA).

papers.title: Tensor Networks Meet Neural Networks: A Survey and Future Perspectives
papers.claim: Surveys 'tensorial neural networks' that combine tensor networks with CNNs, RNNs, Transformers, LLMs and quantum neural networks, covering compression, fusion and efficient training.
papers.relevance: Places TT/Tucker/CP adapters within the wider practice of tensor-network parameterization of neural layers.

notes: Scope: methods whose novelty is the algebraic/tensor-network SHAPE of Delta W beyond plain low rank. 29 methods in 8 sub-families: (1) Hadamard: loha, hira, abba; (2) Kronecker / hypercomplex / Khatri-Rao: lokr, krona, phm-adapter, compacter, kadaptation, kradapter; (3) tensor networks: loretta, tt-lora, lotr, fact, flora-tucker, lorta, metatt, quanta, quantum-peft; (4) square high-rank / block (direct-sum) shapes: mora, melora, gralora, bd-lora; (5) Monarch: more; (6) circulant: c3a; (7) sparse(+low-rank): rosa, dsee, shira; (8) entrywise-nonlinear or replication shapes: sine-lora, miss. Unifying algebra for the category-theory site: Kronecker product = tensor product of linear maps, so rank(A (x) B) = rank A * rank B (LoKr, KronA; MoRA's reshape variant is I (x) M); a sum of n Kronecker products has Kronecker rank n, i.e. ordinary rank n after the Van Loan-Pitsianis rearrangement, so PHM/KAdaptation are 'low rank in another matricization'; Hadamard product = Kronecker product restricted to the diagonal, A o B = J^T (A (x) B) J with J the diagonal embedding, hence rank(A o B) <= rank A * rank B (LoHa, HiRA, ABBA) and the row-wise Khatri-Rao factorization ABBA uses; Khatri-Rao = column-wise Kronecker (KRAdapter); block-diagonal = direct sum of maps (MELoRA, BD-LoRA, MoRA); a circulant is an intertwiner of the cyclic group's regular representation, diagonalized by the DFT (C3A is dual to FourierFT); TT, Tucker and CP adapters are string diagrams in FinVect with trainable boxes, differing only in the graph of contractions (chain, star, hyperedge). A useful invariant across the family is the rank of Delta W under a chosen matricization/reshaping, plus whether factors are shared across layers (LoTR, FacT, LoRTA, MetaTT, Compacter, KAdaptation). Ambiguities: 'FLoRA' names at least three different papers (this Tucker-core one, ICLR 2025, retitled 'Maintaining Structural Integrity...'; the gradient-compression Flora of Hao et al.; federated FLoRA), so the id is flora-tucker. ABBA exists (arXiv 2505.14238, retitled 'ABBA-Adapters', ICLR 2026). HiRA has no arXiv version (ICLR 2025 proceedings/OpenReview only). SHiRA is a sparse-selective method included as a seed; it also belongs in a selective/sparse family. BD-LoRA, MiSS and GraLoRA are low-rank-bounded or rank-k*r but included because their novelty is the shape constraint (block-diagonal, replication, block grid). Unverified details (medium confidence): initialization of MoRe, LoRTA, MetaTT, Quantum-PEFT and KAdaptation was not stated in the sections read; TT-LoRA's venue is from IEEE Xplore/Semantic Scholar (ICMLA 2024) and it does NOT start from the identity; LoRETTA's compensation of random init is paraphrased. Omitted for low uptake or because they duplicate a listed shape: Block Circulant Adapter (BCA, Ding et al., IJCAI 2025, arXiv 2505.00582; same block-circulant shape as C3A plus a learning-rate heuristic), DoTA (TT init from pretrained weights), TLoRA / transformed low-rank via tensor decomposition (ICCV 2025, arXiv 2501.08727), LSR-Adapt (Kronecker-sum kernels), SoKA (SVD on Kronecker adaptation), TT-LoRA MoE, Kron-LoRA. Hadamard Adapter (CIKM 2023, arXiv 2407.11033) is an activation-scaling method that belongs with (IA)^3, not here. Orthogonal butterfly/Householder methods (BOFT, OFT, HRA) and random-basis methods (VeRA, RandLoRA) and spectral FourierFT belong to other families and appear only as relation targets.
